question: Controlled: what does the pepM pre-screen cost and change, one taxon, one code version?
method: 344 Pantoea ananatis genomes taken from the Erwiniaceae download, run through --workflow bgc_analysis twice on branch reference-distances, identical except pepm_prescreen. GTDB-Tk off. Params passed in a JSON file, never on the CLI: `--pepm_prescreen false` arrives as the string "false", which is truthy, and would have silently left the screen on. Timings are per-task realtime x cpus from the Nextflow cache (tasks_*.tsv); the runs failed at AGGREGATE_TAXONOMY, which is after all detection work and does not affect these numbers.
not_perfectly_neutral: 4 of 226 BGCs each lost one RECOVERED gene with the screen on (3,227 -> 3,223 CDS). BUILD_PROTEIN_POOL draws its homology evidence from the screened genomes only - 193 instead of 344, 16,535 instead of 45,358 recovered genes overall - so recovery is slightly weaker. The BGC sequences are identical; the annotation on four of them is not. Affected: Pantoea_ananatis 117T1, PANS_02-01, PNA_98-11, SK-1.
why_the_saving_is_smaller_than_on_erwini: This taxon is phosphonate-rich: 193 of 344 genomes (56%) carry a pepM, against 307 of 2,771 (11%) for Erwiniaceae. The screen pays off in proportion to how dilute the taxon is, so 1.7x here and 6.5x there are both real.
